title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment, Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Comprehensive reference for deploying Redwood Private in customer VPCs and on-prem environments. Covers reference architectures, packaging and installation options, day-2 operational procedures, and tested upgrade/rollback playbooks. Includes customer requirements checklist used by Solutions Engineering during presales and onboarding.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates our recommended practices for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for Solutions Engineering, SRE, and the Private Deployments team owning customer installs. Use this as the canonical reference for architecture decisions, operational runbooks, and the customer requirements library used for scoping.

Scope
- Supported deployment modes: Customer VPC (cloud-hosted private control plane + in-VPC data plane) and fully on-prem (air-gapped option available).
- Components covered: control plane, data plane (inference pods, autoscaler), storage (artifact registry, model store), networking, KMS/HSM integration, observability stack, and packaging options (Kubernetes helm charts, OVA for on-prem, bare-metal systemd).
- Not covered: hosted API operational runbooks (see hosted-api-runbooks) or customer-managed model training pipelines.

Reference Architectures (high level)

1) VPC Deployment (recommended for most customers)
- Topology: Redwood-managed public control plane, customer-managed VPC with private subnets for data plane.
- Key components in customer VPC: NAT gateway, private EKS/GKE/AKS cluster(s), dedicated GPU node pools (pools per model/latency class), internal ALB/NLB for routing, S3-compatible object store for model artifacts, KMS integration (customer master keys), and VPC peering or PrivateLink for control plane connectivity.
- Security controls: private endpoints only, host-based firewall rules, RBAC via OIDC/ICAM, egress controls to restrict external model downloads.
- Sizing guidance: start with 4 GPU nodes for a production pilot (e.g., 4 x A10G or 4 x H100 depending on model family); scale pools based on throughput tests in the benchmarking playbook.

2) On-Prem Deployment (air-gapped or partially connected)
- Topology: Customer datacenter Kubernetes cluster (or on-prem VM cluster). Optional air-gap mode using tarball artifacts and a local container registry.
- Packaging: OVA for quick proof-of-concept; Helm charts and node agents for production installs.
- Hardware: GPUs connected via NVLink preferred for large-context models. Local NFS/CEPH or object-store for model artifacts; recommended model-launch throughput: 1 GB/s+ for concurrent restarts.

Packaging and Prerequisites

Prereqs checklist (customer-facing)
1) Cloud infra: VPC with private subnets, route tables, NAT/egress infrastructure.
2) Kubernetes: 1.25+ (prefer 1.27+), CNI plugin certified, Pod security / OCI runtime configured.
3) GPUs: drivers and CUDA toolkit matching runtime images (see compatibility table).
4) Storage: S3-compatible bucket + IAM role or on-prem object store with credentials.
5) Networking: DNS resolution, internal LB, control plane connectivity (PrivateLink or HTTPS egress on port 8443).
6) Security: customer KMS/HSM integration plan, audit logging enabled, TLS certs for internal services.

Compatibility (example)
- Kubernetes: 1.25 - 1.27 (recommended 1.27).
- CUDA drivers: 11.8 - 12.x (match runtime image: rwinference/runtime:2026-03).
- Helm: 3.8+.
- Supported OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or RHEL 8/9 for bare-metal.

Example packaging commands
- Helm (preferred):
  helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood.ai/helm && helm repo update
  helm upgrade --install redwood-private redwood/redwood-private -n redwood --create-namespace \n    --set image.tag=2026-03 --set controlPlane.endpoint=<cp-endpoint> --set storage.s3.bucket=<bucket>

- Air-gap installation (on-prem):
  1) Transfer artifacts: redwood-private-2026-03.tar.gz to local registry host.
  2) Load images: ctr images import redwood-private-2026-03.tar.gz
  3) Apply manifests from the local helm chart after updating imagePullSecrets.

Deployment procedure (VPC) - pre-deploy -> deploy -> validate

Pre-deploy checklist (ops)
1) Confirm IAM roles and least-privilege policies for cluster nodes and operator.
2) Verify KMS and audit logging endpoints are reachable from the control plane.
3) Ensure GPU drivers and device plugin daemons are installed on target nodes.
4) Confirm NLB/ALB target groups and appropriate health checks (HTTP 200 on /healthz).
5) Reserve CIDR and security group rules for cross-account PrivateLink if used.

Deploy steps (summary)
1) Create namespace: kubectl create ns redwood
2) Install CRDs and operator: helm upgrade --install redwood-operator <chart> -n redwood
3) Apply cluster role bindings and OIDC mappings.
4) Provision model-store (S3) access and test read/write.
5) Scale initial inference pool to warm model caches: kubectl scale deployment/model-pool --replicas=3

Validation (post-deploy)
- Smoke tests: health endpoints, tokenized request roundtrip, and sample inference latency within SLO.
- Observability checks: Prometheus targets up, logs forwarded to customer SIEM, traces visible in Jaeger/OTel.

Day-2 Operations

Monitoring & Alerts
- Minimum dashboards to configure: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), request throughput, GPU utilization per node, model load time, KV cache hit rate, and error rates (4xx/5xx).
- Recommended alerts: p95 latency > 300 ms for latency-SLO routes; GPU memory pressure > 85% for 5 minutes; node readiness flapping > 3 occurrences in 10 minutes.

Scaling and Autoscaling
- Autoscaler setup: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler for CPU-bound controllers, custom scaler for GPU pools (scale by node group).
- Batching policy: batching window 10-20 ms for latency-sensitive traffic; larger windows for asynchronous bulk jobs.

Model lifecycle operations
- Model pinning: always pin model versions in production manifests (e.g., modelRef: redwood/llm-2.1:2026-02).
- KV cache regeneration: perform rolling restart on model-pool with graceful drain to avoid large cold-start spikes.
- Canary rollout: route 5% traffic to new model variant for 24-48 hours; monitor quality metrics and error budget.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

Principles
- Upgrades are staged: dev -> staging -> canary -> prod. Automated smoke tests and evaluation suites gate progression.
- Maintain immutable model images and operator versions for deterministic rollback.

Upgrade procedure (operator or runtime)
1) Prepare release notes and impact matrix covering teams, SLOs, and incompatibilities.
2) Dev/staging validation: run end-to-end smoke tests including inference correctness and performance.
3) Canary: roll operator and runtime to a small subset of clusters or node pools and run synthetic load for 4 hours.
4) Promote when canary meets thresholds (latency, error rate, model quality).
5) Notify customer and schedule broad rollout during maintenance window.

Rollback procedure (fast rollback)
1) If post-upgrade signals breach SLOs (p95 latency increase > 30% or error rate > 3x baseline) trigger rollback.
2) Execute helm rollback: helm rollback redwood-private <previous-release> --wait
3) Restore pinned model images and restart affected model pools with graceful drain disabled to accelerate recovery.
4) Post-rollback: collect diagnostic logs, open an incident where needed, and run regression triage.

Controlled failover (customer DR)
- For cross-region VPC customers, automatic fallback to a secondary region is configured via smart routing policy. For on-prem, configure DNS weight-based failover with health checks against /healthz.

Operational runbooks (quick links)
- Node GPU OOM: cordon node -> delete pods -> reboot driver daemonset -> uncordon.
- Model memory leak: scale down model pool, capture heapdump, open JIRA with priority P1.
- Control plane disconnect: verify VPN/PrivateLink and restart data-plane-agent if control-plane heartbeat missing > 2 minutes.

Customer Requirements Library (for Solutions Engineering)

Minimum information to collect during scoping call (checklist)
1) Environment type: cloud VPC or on-prem (air-gapped?).
2) Expected QPS and latency SLO by route (e.g., chat: p95 < 250 ms, embed: p95 < 100 ms).
3) Peak concurrent active sessions and model concurrency expectations.
4) GPU families available (A10G, T4, A100, H100) and quantities.
5) Network egress/ingress constraints and IP allowlist requirements.
6) KMS/HSM provider, required key rotation cadence and export policy.
7) Compliance regimes: SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA, PCI (affects audit log retention and architecture).
8) Backup/DR requirements and RTO/RPO targets.

Example customer requirement matrix (textual)
- Customer: Acme Finance
  - Environment: VPC (AWS)
  - Target SLO: chat p95 200 ms, embeddings p95 80 ms
  - GPUs: 8 x A10G in one cluster, 4 x A100 in another for batch jobs
  - Compliance: SOC2 + HIPAA, requires HSM for key ops
  - Observability: Send logs to Splunk, traces to OTel collector

Ownership, SLAs and Communication
- Primary owners: Private Deployments (onboarding) - eng-private-deployments@s.redwood.ai; SRE owns production runbooks and monitoring thresholds.
- Escalation path: Oncall SRE -> Private Deployments lead -> Product Security for compliance escalations.
- Typical onboarding timeline: 4-8 weeks for VPC pilot, 8-16 weeks for full on-prem enterprise installs (hardware procurement often drives schedule).

Appendix (snippets & examples)
- Sample Kubernetes toleration and GPU device plugin snippet:
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: PodSpec
  tolerations:
    - key: nvidia.com/gpu
      operator: Exists
      effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
    - name: inference
      image: registry.redwood.ai/rwinference/runtime:2026-03
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/gpu: "1"

- Example helm values excerpt for model-store:
  storage:
    s3:
      endpoint: https://s3.amazonaws.com
      bucket: redwood-models-prod
      credentialsSecret: redwood-s3-creds

Troubleshooting checklist (fast triage)
1) Check operator logs in redwood-operator namespace.
2) Is node GPU kubelet reporting device plugin ready? kubectl get nodes -o wide
3) Check model store connectivity with curl or aws s3 ls using service account credentials.
4) Verify image pull and registry accessibility for air-gap installs.

Change history and governance
- This page is owned by eng-private-deployments. All production-changing runbooks must be reviewed by SRE and Security. Major changes require a cross-team review and signoff (reviewers listed above).
